The CORS policy is set in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`, in the `app.use('*', cors({...}))` middleware. Its `origin` option is a function, and it returns the request's origin only in these cases:

- **Exact match:** `http://localhost:4200`.
- **Suffix match:** any origin that ends with `.pages.dev`, at any depth.
- **Suffix match:** any origin that ends with `.workers.dev`, at any depth.
- **Everything else:** requests with no `Origin` header, or any other origin, get `null`, so no CORS headers are sent.

The same middleware allows these methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`. It allows the headers `Content-Type` and `Authorization`, and sets `maxAge` to 86400.

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `origin` function at `worker/src/index.ts:21-31`. Add a new clause to the `if` condition at lines 23-27:

- For one exact origin, add `origin === 'https://app.example.com' ||`.
- For a whole domain, add `origin.endsWith('.example.com') ||`.

The origin must include the scheme, for example `https://`. A bare `endsWith` check is loose. `.example.com` won't match `evil-example.com`, but a suffix without the leading dot would. Prefer the exact-match form where you can.

Don't put the domain in an array. The code comment and `worker/src/index.md:24-25` both say Hono matches array entries as exact strings, so wildcards only work in the function form. `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 covers CORS in more detail. I didn't open it.

If you change this, update the CORS line in `worker/src/index.md:7` as well. Also redeploy the Worker, because the policy is in code, not in `wrangler.toml`.
